_comment: Word banks and sentence-frame templates for the fully-procedural floor narrative generator (scripts/lib/level-gen/StoryGenerator.mjs, JournalBuilder.mjs). Templates use {slot} placeholders filled from this same category's other arrays, so output stays thematically consistent rather than mad-lib random. Add a themeCategory here and it's immediately available via data/floors-manifest.json's themeCategory field.

arcTemplates: {threat} sealed something down here that was never meant to finish brewing, and the seals are failing.
A formula for {threat} to end all suffering - or all resistance - was hidden in the {domain} below, and someone just found the first ingredient.
{threat} has been using this floor to distill something out of captives who never leave.
subStoryTemplates: A cache of unstable reagents is destabilizing nearby rooms and needs to be found before it detonates.
One of {threat}'s apprentices wants out and has been leaving coded warnings for anyone who'll listen.
A half-transmuted survivor is trapped between forms in a side chamber, begging for the process to be reversed or finished.
The floor's water supply has been dosed with a reagent that's slowly changing everything that drinks it.
friendlyNpcHooks: A former apprentice of {threat} who fled mid-formula and has been hiding here ever since, desperate for someone to finish what they started - or stop it.
A half-transmuted survivor, more lucid than they look, who knows the layout of {threat}'s workshops better than anyone still willing to talk about them.
detailTemplates: A faint chemical tang clings to everything, sharp enough to sting at the back of the throat.
Runnels in the floor channel some old spill toward a drain that hasn't worked in a long time.
Glassware, some of it still faintly warm, lies abandoned mid-experiment.
castTemplates: {name}, a former apprentice who still wears their guild sash out of habit, mixing reagents nobody asked for anymore.
{name}, a lab-rat turned unnervingly loyal familiar after one experiment too many, still answering to a name it probably shouldn't remember.
sideQuestTemplates: A crate of mislabeled reagents has been swapped with a crate of mundane vegetables, and neither side has noticed yet - sorting out which crate is which before someone drinks from the wrong one is trivial, but nobody else seems inclined to do it.
{cast} insists a particular shade of blue means a batch is ruined and a particular shade of green means it's perfect, and can't remember which shade is which - has been guessing for weeks.
Something in the {domain} has started fermenting rather than distilling, and the smell alone is now a bigger problem than the original formula ever was.
A junior alchemist bet their whole stipend that a particular reagent would explode if shaken exactly right, and is now trying to recruit test subjects.
breatherTemplates: A shelf of failed experiments sits labeled, in careful handwriting, "DO NOT." Nobody has followed the instruction in some time.
Chalk equations cover one wall, corrected and re-corrected in three different hands.
A cracked retort has been repurposed as a plant pot for something that probably shouldn't be growing indoors.

secretPayloads.leverage: A partially-legible formula that, properly read, identifies the single unstable compound {threat}'s entire operation depends on.
secretPayloads.payoff: If the party understood the unstable-compound formula, they can threaten to destabilize it in front of {threat} - a credible bluff (or a real one) that buys hesitation, a surrender, or a bargaining position instead of a straight fight.

secretPayloads.leverage: A ledger of debts {threat} owes to guild suppliers who were never paid - proof the operation is one bad delivery away from total collapse.
secretPayloads.payoff: Presenting the ledger to {threat} mid-confrontation forces a choice between the fight and the funding - a distracted or divided {threat} is a noticeably easier one.

promptedFlavorTemplates: If asked what the smell is: "That's not supposed to still be doing that."
If asked who's in charge here: nobody in the room actually knows - {threat} delegates everything and remembers none of it.

arcTemplates: {threat} never got the burial it was owed, and it intends to make everyone still breathing understand why that matters.
Something in the {domain} below is calling the recently dead home, one grave at a time.
{threat} has been rebuilding an army out of everyone who's ever died on this floor - including, eventually, the party.
subStoryTemplates: A restless spirit will not move on until an old debt, owed for generations, is finally settled.
Grave robbers hired by someone topside are already down here, and they know things about the layout the party doesn't.
A single still-living prisoner has been kept alive for decades as a witness to something {threat} doesn't want forgotten - or remembered.
Bones are going missing from sealed tombs, one at a time, in a pattern that spells out a name.
friendlyNpcHooks: The single still-living prisoner {threat} has kept as a witness for decades, finally free enough to talk if someone will listen.
A grave robber who turned back after seeing what {threat} does to the freshly dead, and hasn't stopped feeling watched since.
detailTemplates: Cold radiates from the walls in a way no draft can explain.
Dust lies undisturbed except for a single set of tracks, too fresh for how old this place looks.
Every surface bears a name, scratched by hand, in more languages than should have ever met down here.
castTemplates: {name}, a spirit who insists on proper introductions before anything else, and grows genuinely offended when skipped.
{name}, the last member of the garrison who still remembers being alive, and would very much like someone to talk to about it.
sideQuestTemplates: {cast} has misplaced something - a ring, a name, a single memory - and won't move on until it's found, though the search itself is entirely harmless.
A string of graves has been rearranged into a message no one still living can read, and {threat} isn't the one doing it.
Something down here keeps sweeping the floor with meticulous, pointless care, and has done so for what is very obviously centuries.
A single candle in the {domain} has been burning without fuel for as long as anyone remembers, and someone left a note asking that it never be blown out.
breatherTemplates: A row of small offerings - coins, flowers long since turned to dust, a child's toy - line one wall, undisturbed.
Names are carved into every surface here, patient and unhurried, as if whoever did it had all the time in the world. They did.
A chair sits facing the wall, as though someone were meant to return and sit in it.

secretPayloads.leverage: The true, forgotten name {threat} answered to while it was still alive - the one thing it has never stopped listening for.
secretPayloads.payoff: Speaking {threat}'s true name aloud during the confrontation visibly rattles it - a moment of hesitation the party can use, or, chosen carefully, a chance to actually reach whoever it used to be.

secretPayloads.leverage: A record of the exact grievance that kept {threat} from resting - who wronged it, and how.
secretPayloads.payoff: Confronting {threat} with the truth of its own grievance, rather than a weapon, opens a path to ending this without a fight - though it may cost the party something to make good on the debt themselves.

promptedFlavorTemplates: If asked why it's so cold: it isn't, not really - something here just doesn't remember what warmth felt like, and neither, now, does the air.
If asked whether the dead here are dangerous: most aren't, not on purpose - {threat} is the exception, not the rule.

arcTemplates: {threat} bound a piece of the raw elemental plane into this floor's foundations, and the binding is cracking room by room.
The {domain} below were built to contain {threat} - they were never built to contain it forever.
{threat} is trying to widen a rift that's already reshaping the floor's geography one tremor at a time.
subStoryTemplates: A containment ward is failing in a side chamber and someone needs to re-anchor it before the whole floor destabilizes.
Local wildlife has been mutating near the rift and is now aggressively territorial in ways it wasn't before.
An engineer who helped build the original wards left instructions for shutting it all down - if anyone can find them.
{threat} has agents already on this floor trying to accelerate the breach rather than stop it.
friendlyNpcHooks: The engineer who helped build the original containment wards, still down here trying to finish the shutdown alone.
A refugee from a deeper level fleeing {threat}'s spreading rift, grateful for company and full of warnings.
detailTemplates: Heat and cold trade places in the air without warning, like the room can't decide what season it wants to be.
Fine cracks web the walls, and something bright is visible moving inside a few of them.
The floor is warm underfoot in patches with no obvious source.
castTemplates: {name}, an engineer's apprentice left behind when the original crew fled, still recalibrating instruments nobody's read in years.
{name}, a small elemental spark that's gone domestic, following whoever feeds it interesting minerals.
sideQuestTemplates: {cast} has been trying to teach the local wildlife to fear fire again, with limited and occasionally combustible success.
A gauge in the {domain} has been climbing steadily for weeks, and whoever was supposed to check it stopped showing up.
A vein of raw elemental material has fused two mundane objects together in a way nobody can explain, and someone wants it back regardless.
{threat}'s agents left behind a genuinely excellent packed lunch, untouched, in their hurry - and someone's still hoping to reclaim it.
breatherTemplates: Scorch marks and frost patterns overlap on the same wall, neither one recent enough to explain the other.
A cracked gauge sits frozen mid-reading, its needle pointed at a number nobody wants to think too hard about.
Someone left a windbreak of stacked stone here, clearly built in a hurry and clearly still standing.

secretPayloads.leverage: The original containment ward's activation sigil, still legible, that {threat} never thought to look for because it was never meant to still exist.
secretPayloads.payoff: Redrawing the activation sigil during the confrontation can briefly re-engage part of the original containment around {threat} - not enough to end the fight outright, but enough to blunt its worst effect for a few crucial rounds.

secretPayloads.leverage: A schematic showing the exact structural weak point {threat} has been carefully avoiding damaging itself.
secretPayloads.payoff: Striking the weak point from the schematic, rather than {threat} directly, can force an opening, a retreat, or a much shorter fight than the party was expecting.

promptedFlavorTemplates: If asked what's causing the tremors: nothing good, and it's getting worse the deeper the party goes.
If asked whether the heat or cold is dangerous on its own: not yet - {threat} is still the actual problem, this is just the weather it brings with it.

threats: a splinter sect of the Hollow Star
arcTemplates: {threat} has been using this floor's {domain} for a ritual that requires exactly one more willing - or unwilling - participant.
{threat} believes something asleep beneath the {domain} is a god, and they intend to wake it whether or not that's true.
A schism inside {threat} has turned this floor into a battleground between two versions of the same faith.
subStoryTemplates: A captured initiate wants to defect and can name every trap between here and the inner sanctum - for a price.
Ritual components are being smuggled in from the surface, and cutting off the supply would stall the whole plan.
One of {threat}'s own has started having doubts and is leaving evidence behind, half hoping to be stopped.
A relic central to the ritual has already been stolen by someone with their own agenda, and neither side has noticed yet.
friendlyNpcHooks: A captured initiate of {threat} who wants to defect and can name every trap between here and the inner sanctum - for a price.
One of {threat}'s own, quietly having doubts, who's been leaving evidence behind half hoping someone will stop this.
detailTemplates: Candle wax has pooled and reset so many times it's built its own small landscape on the floor.
A chant, too faint to make out clearly, seems to come from every direction at once and none of them.
Robes hang on pegs along one wall, sized for everyone from children to giants.
castTemplates: {name}, a devotee who still believes completely, and finds the party's skepticism more sad than threatening.
{name}, a former true believer who's since gone quiet about all of it, and flinches at the sight of a robe.
sideQuestTemplates: {cast} needs one more voice for tonight's chant to sound "complete" and is genuinely, harmlessly desperate to recruit anyone within earshot.
A ritual candle in the {domain} has gone out three nights running, and whoever's responsible for relighting it is too afraid of a bad omen to go near it.
Someone has been quietly replacing the sacramental wine with regular wine, and the difference has gone entirely unnoticed for weeks.
A junior member of {threat} lost the ceremonial mask and has been wearing a convincing paper substitute, hoping no one looks too closely.
breatherTemplates: An altar here is dressed for a ceremony that clearly isn't happening today - candles unlit, offerings untouched.
A hand-copied hymnal lies open, its margins full of someone's doodles rather than notes.
A robe several sizes too large hangs alone on its own peg, like it's still waiting for whoever it was meant for.

secretPayloads.leverage: The true wording of the ritual {threat} is building toward - proof it doesn't do what {threat} has told every follower it will do.
secretPayloads.payoff: Reciting the ritual's true wording back at {threat} in front of its own followers can crack the operation's authority wide open, right when it matters most.

secretPayloads.leverage: A signed confession from {threat} admitting the whole thing started as a scheme, not a revelation.
secretPayloads.payoff: Producing the confession at the right moment can turn {threat}'s own followers against it mid-confrontation, buying the party an opening they didn't have to fight for.

promptedFlavorTemplates: If asked what they actually believe: most of them can't fully explain it, and get uncomfortable when pressed - only {threat} claims full certainty.
If asked if the ritual is real: something is definitely happening down here. Whether it's what {threat} thinks is happening is a different question.

threats: something that was never meant to breed this fast
arcTemplates: {threat} has claimed the {domain} below as territory, and it's been expanding its range every season since.
Something in the {domain} triggered a breeding surge, and {threat} now controls far more ground than any survey accounts for.
{threat} isn't hostile by nature - it's defending a nest, and anyone who reaches it uninvited won't get a warning.
subStoryTemplates: A trapper who knows the den layout will trade that knowledge for help freeing a snared partner.
Something is picking off {threat}'s own brood one at a time, and it isn't the party.
A previous expedition's survivor has been living off the land down here long enough to have gone a little feral themselves.
The nest's growth is undermining a structural support that could collapse a much larger section of the floor.
friendlyNpcHooks: A trapper who knows the den layout and will trade that knowledge for help freeing a snared partner.
A previous expedition's survivor who's lived off this land long enough to have gone a little feral themselves, but still remembers how to talk.
detailTemplates: Claw marks, old and new, mark every doorway at roughly chest height.
The air smells thickly of animal musk and something recently killed.
Bones, cracked for marrow, are scattered with the casualness of a well-used feeding ground.
castTemplates: {name}, a trapper who's spent so long down here they've started thinking in the same patterns as what they're tracking.
{name}, a juvenile beast too young to be properly territorial yet, more curious than dangerous - for now.
sideQuestTemplates: {cast} has a snare that's caught the wrong thing three times running, and would appreciate help resetting it properly before it happens a fourth time.
A den in the {domain} has been abandoned mid-litter, and the young left behind are too young to fend for themselves.
Something has been leaving small, deliberate gifts of food outside a particular chamber, and nobody's figured out who - or what - it's trying to befriend.
{threat}'s territory marking has started overlapping with a much smaller, much less dangerous animal's, and the smaller one is losing badly.
breatherTemplates: A nest built from scavenged cloth and bits of old armor sits empty in one corner, recently abandoned.
Deep scratches mark a rough tally into the stone - feeding days, maybe, or something else entirely.
A trail of disturbed earth leads nowhere in particular and doubles back on itself twice.

secretPayloads.leverage: A scent-marked hide that, worn or carried, reads to {threat} as belonging to something it already submits to.
secretPayloads.payoff: Carrying or wearing the marked hide during the confrontation can trigger {threat}'s instinct to submit rather than fight - briefly, and only if the deception isn't pushed too far.

secretPayloads.leverage: The exact location of {threat}'s actual young, kept separate from the den the party has already found.
secretPayloads.payoff: Threatening or protecting the real nest, once found, gives the party leverage {threat} will not risk ignoring, regardless of how the fight is otherwise going.

promptedFlavorTemplates: If asked why the animals down here act strangely: {threat} isn't hostile by nature, it's defending something, and everything nearby has picked up the same instinct.
If asked whether this can be avoided entirely: probably, if the party doesn't push into the den itself - but the stairs down don't care about that.

threats: something that predates the floor itself
a presence with no true name
arcTemplates: {threat} was sealed in the {domain} long before this floor was ever mapped, and the seal was never meant to last this long.
{threat} doesn't want anything from the party - it wants them to stop looking, and it's willing to rearrange the floor to make that happen.
Something about the {domain} below makes maps stop matching the territory, and {threat} is the reason why.
subStoryTemplates: A previous survey team's final log entries describe something that shouldn't be believed - and shouldn't be ignored either.
A sealed door has no lock, no hinges, and no explanation, and something on the other side has started answering knocks.
One party member's dreams have started including rooms that don't exist yet on this floor's map - until they do.
{threat} has been testing the wards a little more each night, and tonight is the first time one of them didn't hold.
friendlyNpcHooks: The sole survivor of a previous expedition's final log entries, alive but changed by however long they've spent near {threat}.
Someone whose dreams started including rooms that don't exist on this floor's map yet - until they do - and who wants that to stop.
detailTemplates: Sound behaves wrong here - footsteps land a half-second late, or not at all.
The dark isn't merely unlit; light behaves like it's being spent rather than simply blocked.
A cold that has nothing to do with temperature settles into anyone who lingers too long.
castTemplates: {name}, the last member of a previous expedition, present but not entirely all here anymore.
{name}, who insists they've done this exact conversation before, word for word, and isn't wrong.
sideQuestTemplates: {cast} keeps finding the same coin over and over, in different rooms, and is quietly convinced it's the same coin every time.
A door in the {domain} has started answering knocks that nobody sent - it isn't hostile, or hasn't been yet, but it is definitely listening.
Someone's old camp is still set up exactly as they left it, mid-meal, with no explanation for where they went.
A journal entry describes tomorrow's events in exact, unsettling detail - and today's date matches.
breatherTemplates: A stretch of wall here doesn't quite match the map, by a measurement too small to be sure of and too consistent to dismiss.
Every echo in this room returns a half-second wrong, like the space is slightly larger than it looks.
A cold spot lingers here with no draft to explain it, exactly the width of a doorway that isn't there.

secretPayloads.leverage: A previous expedition's working theory that {threat} can be genuinely startled by a truth it doesn't already know - paired with a truth the party has since learned that it plainly doesn't.
secretPayloads.payoff: Stating the one true thing {threat} doesn't already know, mid-confrontation, causes a visible, useful disruption - the only known crack in its composure.

secretPayloads.leverage: Evidence that {threat} is bound to this floor by something physical and mundane, not by anything cosmic at all.
secretPayloads.payoff: Destroying or removing the mundane binding object, once identified, meaningfully weakens {threat} for the remainder of the encounter.

promptedFlavorTemplates: If asked what {threat} wants: nothing the party can give it directly - it wants them gone, and unaware, and is willing to rearrange quite a lot to manage both.
If asked if the floor's map can be trusted: less and less, the deeper they go.

threats: a goblin war-band that's crowned a llama as their living god
the Wool-Crowned King and his stolen throne of saddlebags
a llama cavalry that never agreed to be a cavalry
two goblin chiefs feuding over which of them the llamas actually like better
arcTemplates: {threat} has turned the {domain} into equal parts throne room and petting zoo, and nobody currently in charge can explain how that happened.
Somewhere in the {domain}, {threat} is handing out promotions based entirely on who the llamas nuzzle first.
{threat} started as a joke - a goblin sat on a llama once, on a dare - and now it's the closest thing this warren has to a government.
subStoryTemplates: A goblin quartermaster is trying to smuggle out the good llama, the one that doesn't spit on command, before the war-band notices it's gone.
Two rival goblin chiefs have agreed to settle their feud with a llama race down the main hall - and both have been caught trying to bribe the same llama.
One llama has figured out that spitting on goblins gets it double rations, and has started training the others.
A goblin who fell off a llama during the coronation still hasn't lived it down, and is looking for literally anyone new to tell the story to.
friendlyNpcHooks: A goblin cook who's stopped asking questions about the chain of command as long as somebody keeps bringing hay.
A llama who wandered in from a passing caravan months ago and has since - through no effort of its own - become a folk hero.
detailTemplates: A goblin somewhere nearby is loudly, badly, singing something about llamas.
Wool tufts drift across the floor like fallen leaves, caught in every corner and crevice.
Hoofprints and boot-prints overlap so thickly here that this is clearly a route, not a destination.
castTemplates: {name}, a goblin scribe who takes the warren's llama-based bureaucracy with total, unblinking seriousness.
{name}, a llama who has, through no effort of its own, become the center of an entire chain of command.
sideQuestTemplates: {cast} is trying to get a promotion by any means necessary and has started asking literally everyone, including the party, for tips on llama etiquette.
Somebody's been forging entries on the warren's nuzzle-ranking board, and the goblins are one bad accusation away from a genuine civil war over it.
A llama has wandered off into the {domain} unsupervised, and its herder is far more panicked about this than the situation seems to warrant.
Two goblins are in the middle of a very serious, very stupid duel over who gets to hold the ceremonial hay-fork, and both would love an excuse to stop.
breatherTemplates: A pile of the warren's finest bedding - by warren standards - has been claimed, unofficially, by a napping llama nobody's brave enough to move.
A hand-lettered sign warns against several very specific things, all involving llamas, all clearly learned the hard way.
Someone has tried, and failed, to teach a llama to guard this spot. The llama is asleep.

secretPayloads.leverage: Proof of exactly how {threat} first came to power - less a coronation, more an accident nobody's corrected.
secretPayloads.payoff: Reciting the true, embarrassing origin story out loud in front of {threat}'s own followers can undercut its authority at exactly the wrong moment for it.

secretPayloads.leverage: The name of the one llama whose approval {threat} has never actually earned - and still, visibly, wants.
secretPayloads.payoff: Bringing that llama into the confrontation, or simply invoking its name, throws {threat} off in a way no weapon has managed.

promptedFlavorTemplates: If asked who's really in charge here: pause before answering. It's genuinely unclear whether it's {threat} or the llamas.
If asked why everyone's so afraid of a llama: they aren't, not exactly - they're afraid of what happens if they're the one it doesn't nuzzle.

entrance: The way down opens into a {adj} chamber, the air already carrying a trace of what waits deeper in the {domain}.
This landing marks the last point where retreat is still simple - past here, the {domain} close in.
corridor-junction: Passages fork here into the {adj} heart of the {domain}, worn smooth by traffic that wasn't always living.
A junction of old routes, {adj} enough that it's clearly seen more use than the maps suggest.
treasure-vault: A {adj} strongroom, its contents undisturbed long enough to have accumulated a history of their own.
Whatever was worth sealing away in this {adj} vault, someone judged it worth more than easy access.
secret-vault: Hidden behind a wall no casual search would find, this {adj} chamber was never meant to be entered twice.
A concealed vault, {adj} and undisturbed - whoever built it wanted it forgotten, not just locked.
boss-arena: The {domain} open into a {adj} hall built - or reshaped - around whatever now claims it as its own.
This is clearly the heart of the floor: {adj}, deliberately spacious, and unmistakably occupied.
hazard-chamber: A {adj} room whose original purpose has been overtaken by something considerably less safe to stand near.
The floor and walls here bear the marks of a hazard that's still active, {adj} as it's become with age.
rest-area: A {adj} alcove, quiet enough that it's clearly been used as a waypoint by more than one previous expedition.
This small chamber is {adj} but defensible - a rare pocket of calm in the {domain}.
chamber: A {adj} room, unremarkable at a glance but part of the {domain}'s larger pattern all the same.
Another {adj} chamber in the {domain}, its purpose only clear in context with what's around it.

hazardTemplates.text: A pressure plate near the threshold triggers a hidden mechanism unless disarmed (DC {dc} to notice, DC {dc} to disarm).
The floor here is unstable and gives way under careless weight (DC {dc} to notice before stepping wrong).
A ward etched into the doorway reacts to anyone who isn't already marked as an ally (DC {dc} to detect and counter).
A residual effect lingers in the air, growing worse the longer anyone stays without taking precautions (DC {dc} to resist each round).

encounterTemplates: Roll a random encounter check when the party lingers here more than a few minutes - something has noticed them.
A patrol or wandering hazard tied to the floor's threat passes through this area on a rotation; a failed Perception check meets it head-on.
This room refills with a new threat if left and returned to later, on the same table used for the floor's other random encounters.
